items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Identity Map: One object per row per request, so repeated reads return the same instance.
Traits: A bundle of methods mixed into classes to share behaviour horizontally.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.

8221.title: Using More Than One Trait
8221.code:
<?php
trait IdentityTrait
{
    public function generateId(): string
    {
        return uniqid();
    }
}
8221.explanation: You can include multiple traits in a class by listing each one after the use keyword, separated by commas. In this example, I define and apply a new trait, IdentityTrait, keeping my original PriceUtilities trait:

8222.title: This means the class offers both the calculateTax() and generateId() methods
8222.code:
<?php
class ShopProduct
{
    use PriceUtilities;
    use IdentityTrait;
}
8222.explanation: By applying both PriceUtilities and IdentityTrait with the use keyword, I make the calculateTax() and the generateId() methods available to the ShopProduct class. This means the class offers both the calculateTax() and generateId() methods.
